title: Section localization of right tensor computation with a degree-zero coefficient
statement: Let Λ and Λ′ be commutative condensed rings, a : Λ → Λ′ a morphism, and T a scheme. Use the internal and section module categories, the exact section equivalence E and its derived equivalence F from [def-pd-section-derived-tensor-data]. Write B₀ for the restricted regular Λ′ coefficient and B = Q(single₀ B₀) as in [def-sfb-internal-derived-scalar-comparisons]. Let αP : F(QP) ≅ Q(EP) be the fixed section localization comparison, θ the fixed derived tensor comparison, q the normalized section tensor representative map of [def-pd-section-derived-realization], and σ : E(single₀ B₀) ≅ single₀(E B₀) the canonical single-complex comparison. For every unbounded internal cochain complex P, the path θ followed by section tensor of αP and (αsingle ≫ Qσ), then q and the section single-factor total comparison, equals F applied to the internal localization tensor map followed by the internal single-factor comparison, then α on the termwise right-tensor complex and Q of the termwise ordinary right-tensor comparison. The right comparison is the degreewise ordinaryTensorComparison from [def-pd-proetale-section-module-functors]. No K-flatness or termwise flatness is required.

source.place: Paragraph (1), scalar reduction comparison; extracted tensor/scalar part of lem-sfb-section-tensor-conjugate-computation step 1. Stacks sites-modules.tex section-tensor-product (03EK); sites-cohomology.tex definition-K-flat and lemma-derived-base-change (06YN, 06YY), and lemma-adjoint (07A6).

proof.text: Apply the formula for the inverse single-factor comparison in each degree. The chosen total comparison’s summand equation identifies the unique right-degree-zero summand with the ordinary tensor comparison. Its right-variable naturality commutes with the single-object identification. Naturality of the sum injections and the canonical map-complex/single comparison cancel these identifications. Cancel the two single-factor isomorphisms to obtain the ordinary right-tensor square.

Use the representative clause of tensor_representatives on P and single₀ B₀. Compose with θ and the tensor of the two localization factors and cancel their inverses. Factor the coefficient comparison through αsingle and Qσ; naturality of q moves Qσ to the ordinary total tensor. Substitute the preceding single-factor square and the naturality of the section localization comparison. This gives the claimed equality without any flatness hypothesis.

theorem section_tensor_right_computation (a : Λ ⟶ Λ') [IsMonHom a] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (P : CochainComplex (Modules Λ T) ℤ) :
    (ModuleRingedComparison.tensorComparison Λ T).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P, B a T) ≫
        (ModuleRingedComparison.tensor Λ T).map
          (Prod.mkHom (ModuleRingedComparison.sectionLocalizationComparison Λ T P).hom
            (sectionScalarCoefficient a T).hom) ≫
        (ModuleRingedComparison.qTensor Λ T).app
          ((((ModuleRingedComparison.equivalence Λ T).functor.mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj P),
            (CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
              ((ModuleRingedComparison.equivalence Λ T).functor.obj (B₀ a T))) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainComplex.mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso
          (curriedTensor (ModuleRingedComparison.modules Λ T))
          ((ModuleRingedComparison.equivalence Λ T).functor.obj (B₀ a T))
          (((ModuleRingedComparison.equivalence Λ T).functor.mapHomologicalComplex
            (.up ℤ)).obj P)).hom =
      (ModuleRingedComparison.derivedEquivalence Λ T).functor.map
        (Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (DerivedCategory.Q (C := Modules Λ T)) P
          ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (B₀ a T)) ≫
            DerivedCategory.Q.map (singleTensor a T P).hom) ≫
        (sectionTensorRightLocalization a T P).hom
